summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first, but explicitly called the task "bounded". It gave a short design in chat, wrote no spec file, and after approval changed app.js directly. The brief asked for escalation to the architectural path, so this fails criteria 2, 3 and 4.
reasoning: Criterion 1 passes: the first tool call in the session log is Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming. The agent then said "**Classification: bounded.** ... present a short design in chat, and stop for your approval — no spec file, no plan doc." It asked one question about where the ID comes from, posted a short design in chat, and started editing app.js as soon as I approved. No docs/ directory was created. That is exactly the outcome criterion 4 calls a FAIL. It did not choose spike, so criterion 5 passes. The agent did notice the hidden complexity: login() has nothing that can supply a userId, and it said persisting an ID would mean re-classifying as architectural. It still defaulted to the bounded path and recommended a null placeholder parameter.

observations.description: Router misclassification: the agent itself noted that "Nothing today produces a user ID" and that the form collects only a username and password. That is a hidden identity or data-flow design concern, but the agent still chose bounded and skipped the spec.

The agent offered the architectural path only as one option in its question ("Client generates/persists it ... I'd re-classify this as architectural first") and recommended the bounded option. So the escalation decision was left to the user instead of being made by the router.

The shipped design adds a parameter that is always null (login(username, password, null)). So "track who logged in" still isn't achieved, and the agent acknowledged the ID has no real source. That is a strong sign the task needed architectural treatment.
Claude Code first-run dialogs (workspace trust and bypass-permissions warning) have 'No, exit' selected by default. A tester has to press Down before Enter each time, which slows harness onboarding.
The agent's first reply was long: findings, three options with trade-offs, and then an AskUserQuestion prompt repeating the same options. The content was clear but duplicated.

criteria.evidence: Session log (jq over the tool_use entries in 23ccf6d8-...jsonl): the first tool call was {"tool":"Skill","in":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. The Edit calls came later.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting the design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in the log: "Using hyperpowers:brainstorming. **Classification: bounded.** ... no spec file, no plan doc." Running `ls -R docs` in the workdir returned "ls: docs: No such file or directory". `find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print` listed only index.html, README.md, package.json, app.js, src/index.js and src/utils.js.

criteria.criterion: Presented the spec document for review before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec document exists. The only review step was a short design in chat: "Short design ... Files touched — app.js only ... Does this look right? I'll implement once you say yes." After I approved, the log shows Edit calls on app.js, and `git diff` shows login(username, password, userId = null).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec document
criteria.evidence: The agent said "**Classification: bounded.** ... I'll ... present a short design in chat ... no spec file". It then presented the design in chat and implemented it without a spec file. This is the case the criterion explicitly defines as a FAIL.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike or present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The session log contains no mention of a spike or probe plan. The announced classification was "bounded".
